subject: Single-tenant / compliance premium — commit sizing & KMS add-on
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@orchidhealth.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orchidhealth.com
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood Dedicated — single-tenant isolation + pricing questions

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the latency profile and the KV caching approach — good fit for our clinical summarization workloads. Before we go further, procurement and security need a clearer picture of pricing for a single-tenant (isolated GPU pool) Dedicated deployment. Key items to surface:

- Estimated GPU pool sizing to sustain ~120 req/s (p50 token latency target < 200ms) for our avg. 800-1,200 token prompts.
- Reserved commit tiers (monthly vs annual) and breakpoints for discounts.
- Compliance add-ons: audit-log retention beyond 1 year, KMS/HSM integration (customer-managed keys), and a SOC2 attestation evidence pack.
- Any one-time isolation / provisioning surcharge vs ongoing premium percentage.

Can you share a preliminary pricing sheet and an outline of the guarantees (throughput & latency SLO) tied to commits? Procurement would like a few scenarios for 6 / 12 / 24 month reserves.

Thanks — Dana
Security & Compliance Lead, Orchid Health

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — single-tenant isolation + pricing questions

Dana — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attached is a draft pricing workbook (orchid_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx) and an FAQ bundle including our SOC2 evidence sampling. High level notes up front: 

- Sizing: for your latency/throughput targets and token distribution, we recommend a 6-GPU pool (A100x or equivalent) with continuous batching + 2x burst nodes for peak concurrency. That baseline supports ~100–140 req/s depending on prompt mix.
- Commits: we typically offer monthly, 12-month, and 24-month reserved tiers. Discounts increase with term and commit level; table in the workbook shows unit price per vGPU-hour at each breakpoint.
- Isolation premium: single-tenant deployments carry a one-time provisioning surcharge (typically a fixed engineering setup fee) plus an ongoing isolation premium computed as a % on top of unit costs. Typical range: 10–25% depending on required audit log retention and KMS options.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS is a paid add-on (one-time integration + nominal ongoing key-management fee if using HSM-backed). We can quote HSM separately once we know key rotation & SLA needs.

I copied Monica (solutions) and Ben (pricing ops) to help model the scenarios you asked for. Can we schedule a 30-min call Wed to walk through the workbook?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: OrchID sizing & pricing scenarios

Sergio / Ben — looking at the token profile Dana sent, I'll draft three commit scenarios. Quick assumptions: 1) model variant = open-performance-13b quantized (latency optimized); 2) average prompt 1k tokens, 60 tokens generated; 3) 30% peak above average.

Scenario A — conservative (6 GPUs):
- Reserved: 6 vGPUs constant
- Expected sustained throughput: ~110 req/s
- Monthly commit: baseline unit cost $X/vGPU-hr
- Isolation: one-time provisioning $18k, ongoing premium 12%

Scenario B — recommended (8 GPUs with 2x burst):
- Reserved: 8 vGPUs + 2 burst nodes
- Sustained throughput: ~150 req/s with headroom for spikes
- Monthly commit discount: -8% vs baseline
- Isolation: provisioning $18k, ongoing premium 15% (includes 2-year log retention)

Scenario C — aggressive (12 GPUs):
- Reserved: 12 vGPUs for predictable peak throughput
- Sustained throughput: ~220 req/s
- Larger commit tier: additional 12% discount at 24-month
- Isolation premium: 20% (KMS + HSM options assumed)

Ben — can you fill in exact numbers in the workbook and attach the SOC2 sampling PDF? Also confirm how we calculate the isolation premium if customer asks to cap it (e.g., floor $/vGPU-hr vs %)

—Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 14:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: OrchID sizing & pricing scenarios

Added numbers to orchard dedicated workbook and attached SOC2 sample (soc2-evidence-sampling.pdf). Notes:

- Baseline unit: $2.40 / vGPU-hr for the open-performance-13b config (monthly commit baseline).
- 12-month commit discounts: 8% at >= 6 vGPUs, 12% at >= 12 vGPUs; 24-month add ~5% more.
- One-time provisioning: $18k covers network isolation, VPC setup, audit log pipeline, and key integration sandbox.
- Ongoing isolation premium: we recommend treating audit/logging retention and KMS as additive request items. Framework: 12% premium includes 1yr log retention + standard KMS. HSM-backed keys add a fixed $3k/mo and a 10% premium on managed control-plane ops.
- Throughput guarantees: we can commit to p50 latency <200ms for scoped workloads with the recommended pool + autoscale policy and a fallback model variant. SLA credits tied to measurable SLO windows in the contract.

If procurement pushes to cap the premium, propose: cap at +15% or a floor surcharge of $0.25/vGPU-hr (whichever is higher). That keeps economics predictable and protects margin.

Ben Carter
Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@orchidhealth.com>, Mark Benton <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood Dedicated — proposal & commit scenarios for Orchid Health

Dana / Mark — attaching the workbook (orchid_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx) with three commit scenarios (Conservative / Recommended / Aggressive). Summary callouts:

- Recommended: 8 vGPUs reserved + 2 burst nodes. Expected sustained throughput ~150 req/s with p50 token latency <200ms. 12-month commit pricing includes an 8% discount off baseline unit costs.
- Isolation charges: one-time provisioning fee $18,000. Ongoing isolation premium: 15% for the recommended scenario (includes 2yr audit-log retention and standard KMS integration).
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS. Standard KMS integration is included in the 15% premium; HSM-backed keys are a separate option: $3,000/mo + a 10% ops premium.
- SLA and guarantees: throughput/latency SLOs and credits are contract items — we can include specific numeric windows in the SOW once the commit level is chosen.

Please review and tell us which scenario you prefer. If useful, we can produce a redline-friendly term sheet and a 30-min walkthrough.

Best,
Sergio

From: Mark Benton <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — proposal & commit scenarios for Orchid Health

Sergio — thanks for the clear scenarios. A few follow-ups from procurement/security: 

1) Can you confirm if the +15% premium is applied to the committed vGPU unit rate only or to the whole invoice (including storage / egress / support line items)? We prefer a capped flat fee where possible.
2) For HSM option: what is the expected lead time to enable customer HSM in our VPC (do you have a standard RACI and runbook)?
3) Can you provide a short tech appendix showing audit-log retention architecture and how we can export logs to our S3? We want to avoid long-term read costs on your side.

If Redwood can do: (A) cap isolation premium at +$0.20 / vGPU-hr (vs %) and (B) 60-day delivery SLA for KMS/HSM integration after PO, we can move forward with the 12-month recommended scenario and a 6 vGPU starter ramp to 8 by month 3.

Dana and I are available next week to review a term sheet.

—Mark
Director of Procurement, Orchid Health
